patches.summary: Added SQLite-backed local store (internal/store/store.go) using modernc.org/sqlite for offline novel features.
patches.reason: The generated file cache (internal/cache/cache.go) is read-only and too simple for the 14 novel commands that need FTS5, session tracking, credit accounting, and cross-command data sharing.

patches.summary: Patched promoted_web.go to persist each live search call to the local SQLite store after API success.
patches.reason: Novel offline features (local-search, drift-detect, corpus gaps, sources-rank, budget-watch, replay) all depend on having prior search results stored locally. Without this hook, the store stays empty.
patches.validated_outcome: After 'web' calls, store.FTSSearch() finds matches; local-search returns results; corpus gaps reports unextracted URLs.

patches.summary: Patched promoted_extract.go to persist each live extract call to the local SQLite store after API success.
patches.reason: freshness-check and corpus gaps need the extraction history to compute stale/missing URLs.

patches.summary: Changed freshness-check --older-than from DurationVar (rejects '7d') to StringVar with custom parseFreshnessDuration helper.
patches.reason: Go's time.ParseDuration does not support the 'd' (days) suffix. Users naturally write '7d', '30d' etc. The generated DurationVar flag silently rejected these with a confusing parse error.
patches.validated_outcome: freshness-check --older-than 7d outputs 'No pages older than 168h0m0s found in cache.' instead of flag parse error.

patches.summary: Hold the AdaptiveLimiter mutex across slot computation in Wait() so concurrent callers serialize through distinct slots.
patches.reason: The generated implementation released the lock between reading lastRequest/rate and writing the new lastRequest, so two goroutines computed the same slot, slept identical durations, and fired together — defeating the limiter and tripping go test -race. Verified with go test -race ./internal/cliutil/...
patches.validated_outcome: go test -race ./internal/cliutil/... passes; concurrent Wait() calls now serialize.

patches.summary: Implemented --query-file reading in `corpus build` (one query per line, '#' comments and blank lines skipped); combined with --query flags instead of erroring.
patches.reason: The generated stub advertised --query-file in --help and the README but returned 'not yet read (add --query as fallback)' when used. Users following the documented usage saw a confusing error.

patches.summary: refreshAccessToken() now returns an actionable error pointing users at TAVILY_API_KEY / `auth set-token` instead of silently letting an expired access_token reach the wire.
patches.reason: The generated stub returned nil unconditionally, so an expired access_token in config produced 3 silent 401 retries with no diagnostic. Tavily uses static API keys; OAuth refresh has no upstream template yet.

patches.summary: Compute the 'today' window for budget-watch and cost-report from local-calendar midnight via startOfLocalDay() instead of time.Now().Truncate(24h).
patches.reason: time.Time.Truncate operates on the absolute instant and snaps to UTC midnight regardless of zone, so 'today' was up to ±12h off for non-UTC users and undercounted same-day spend.

patches.summary: Log store.Open / InsertSearch / InsertExtract / InsertCredit failures to stderr in the `web` and `extract` commands instead of swallowing them.
patches.reason: Silent failures here corrupt downstream offline commands (replay, local-search, corpus gaps, drift-detect, freshness-check) by making them operate on stale data. Disk-full, permission, and SQLite corruption errors are now visible to the user.

patches.summary: Quote bare search terms in FTSSearch/FTSExtract before binding to MATCH so common phrases like 'AI AND ML' don't trip the FTS5 parser.
patches.reason: SQLite's FTS5 parses the bound MATCH value as a query expression; bare AND/OR/NOT/NEAR keywords and stray punctuation produce 'fts5: syntax error near X' instead of empty results. quoteFTSTerm wraps plain prose in phrase quotes and leaves explicit operator syntax (parens, quotes, spaced AND/OR/NOT/NEAR) untouched so the documented FTS5 syntax in --term still works.
patches.validated_outcome: tavily-pp-cli local-search --term 'AI AND ML' returns no-results-message instead of fts5 parse error; --term '(rag OR retrieval) AND llm' still parses as operator syntax.

patches.summary: Wrap store migrate() DDL in a Begin/Commit transaction with explicit rollback on error.
patches.reason: All CREATE statements were batched into one Exec without a tx, so a mid-batch failure (e.g. searches_fts) could leave the searches_ai trigger pointing at a missing virtual table. SQLite does not validate trigger targets at CREATE time, so every subsequent INSERT INTO searches would then fail with 'no such table: searches_fts'. The transaction makes the migration all-or-nothing.

patches.summary: Surface InsertCrawl failures in corpus build to stderr and guard InsertCredit/UpdateCrawlCheckpoint on success so cost-report doesn't over-count crawls that never persisted.
patches.reason: The generated code wrote `crawlID, _ := st.InsertCrawl(...)` and unconditionally charged a 2.0-credit crawl row. When InsertCrawl failed (disk full, SQLite locked), crawlID stayed 0, the credit entry persisted with no matching crawl, and UpdateCrawlCheckpoint silently no-op'd because WHERE id=0 matched nothing — leaving cost-report over-counting and crawl-resume with nothing to resume.
patches.validated_outcome: InsertCrawl errors now print a 'warning: store InsertCrawl ... failed' line; on failure, InsertCredit and UpdateCrawlCheckpoint are skipped so credits and checkpoints stay consistent with persisted crawl rows.

patches.summary: Added 14 novel transcendence commands wired in root.go: qna, context, local-search, corpus (build+gaps), drift-detect, budget-watch, cost-report, batch-plan, replay, freshness-check, crawl-resume, research-track, sources-rank.
patches.reason: These commands leverage the SQLite store to provide capabilities unavailable in any other Tavily client: offline FTS, credit budget management, RAG corpus building, session-based agent replay, and cache freshness management.
